# CMS validated-runs ("golden JSON") for 2016

**File:** `Cert_271036-284044_13TeV_Legacy2016_Collisions16_JSON.txt`

**Do not edit this file.** It is committed verbatim, byte-for-byte, from
the CERN Open Data portal so that cluster jobs do not need network access
to apply the validated-runs filter (`parsing_task_config.validated_runs_json`
in `services/parsing/schemas.py` / `services/parsing/event_selection.py`).
If a newer or different certified-runs list is ever needed, add it as a
new file with its own README entry — do not modify this one in place.

## Source

- **Portal record:** [https://opendata.cern.ch/record/14220](https://opendata.cern.ch/record/14220)
  (API: `https://opendata.cern.ch/api/records/14220`)
- **Record title:** "CMS list of validated runs
  Cert_271036-284044_13TeV_Legacy2016_Collisions16_JSON.txt"
- **Record's own description, quoted verbatim:** "This file describes
  which luminosity sections in which runs are considered good and should
  be processed. This list covers 13TeV proton-proton collision data taken
  in 2016. Run2016G is between run numbers 278820 and 280385. Run2016H is
  between run numbers 280919 and 284044."
- **Coverage claimed by the record's own `run_period` field:**
  `["Run2016B", "Run2016C", "Run2016D", "Run2016E", "Run2016F", "Run2016G", "Run2016H"]`
  — i.e. this is the full-2016 certified-runs list, not one restricted to
  G/H (the DoubleEG eras used by this project's H→γγ study only released
  G and H NanoAOD on the portal — see `studies/hgg_cms/INVENTORY.md` A.1).
- **"Legacy2016" vs. "UL2016" naming, UNVERIFIED beyond the following**:
  the portal record's title and metadata use "Legacy2016", not literally
  "UL2016". CMS's own NanoAOD dataset names for the files this filter is
  meant to be used with are `UL2016_MiniAODv2_NanoAODv9` (Ultra Legacy).
  "Legacy2016" and "UL2016" are the same final 2016 reprocessing campaign
  in standard CMS usage, and the certified-run/lumisection content itself
  does not depend on which downstream reprocessing (MiniAOD/NanoAOD
  version) is being certified — but the portal page does not use the
  string "UL" anywhere in this record's own text, so treat the "Legacy2016
  ≡ UL2016 certification" equivalence as consistent with, but not
  verbatim-stated by, the portal. It is independently cross-checked in
  `studies/hgg_cms/impl_checks/` (see below): this file's own certified
  run/lumisection counts for Run2016G (70 runs, 43,014 sections) and
  Run2016H (86 runs, 47,793 sections) match exactly the `nrun`/`nls`
  columns in the portal's own official per-run luminosity summaries,
  `Run2016Glumi.txt` / `Run2016Hlumi.txt` (record 1059, already used for
  `INVENTORY.md` A.2's luminosity numbers) — strong evidence this is
  indeed the correct list for the UL2016 luminosity already being used.

- 393 runs listed, 523 separate lumisection ranges, 234,231 certified
  lumisections in total (full 2016, all eras).
- Restricted to the Run2016G run-number range quoted above
  (278820–280385): **70 certified runs, 43,014 certified lumisections.**
- Restricted to the Run2016H run-number range quoted above
  (280919–284044): **86 certified runs, 47,793 certified lumisections.**
  (Record 30554's own `run_numbers` list for the actual DoubleEG dataset
  starts later, at run 281613 — but there are zero certified runs in the
  280919–281613 gap either way, so this does not change the count.)

Full analysis script and its JSON output:
`studies/hgg_cms/impl_checks/golden_json_analysis.py` /

## Format

A JSON object. Each key is a run number as a string; each value is a list
of `[first, last]` lumisection-number ranges, both **inclusive**, that are
certified good for that run. Example (first lines of this file):

```json
{
  "273158": [[1, 1283]],
  "273302": [[1, 459]],
  ...
  "273425": [[62, 352], [354, 742]],
  ...
}
```
